packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 11 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of these
fragments before reading. I have not tried to identify any work. Personal names
that appear below ("Pet(rus) damiani", "Petr(us)", "simone mago") are words
written on the parchment, not identifications by me.

====================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)
====================================================================
Two horizontal parchment strips, each pasted on a cloth/leather support (binding
context), each with its own overview:
- Strip A: image-001 (overview); image-002 = left half, image-003 = right half.
- Strip B: image-004 (overview); image-005 = left half, image-006 = right half.

Each strip is upright and consists of two visibly different areas side by side,
separated by a vertical line/seam (at about 57% of the width in strip A, about
46% in strip B):

LEFT AREA (both strips): a larger, widely spaced script in brown ink with small
musical signs (staffless neumes: short oblique strokes, hooks, small loops, dots)
written above every line of text. Drypoint ruling is visible. Sentences begin
with plain enlarged capitals (C, Q, S, E); no colour. Tentative interpretation:
a sung text with notation, in dialogue form (question / answer wording).
In strip B two further lines in a different, smaller, later-looking cursive hand
without notation are added underneath the notated text.

RIGHT AREA (both strips): a smaller, compact, darker script, 11 lines in strip A
and 9 lines in strip B, continuous prose with many abbreviations. Two paragraphs
in strip A begin with an enlarged initial P set out into the left margin. No
rubrics, no underlining, no interlinear glosses. Strip B's right area has a
blank lower margin beneath its last line (with a few thin pen strokes hanging
down), so that is the foot of a column or page.

I cannot tell from the images whether left and right areas are two columns of
one leaf written by different hands, two pages of an opening across a fold, or
two separate pieces mounted together; the vertical line between them could be a
fold, a column boundary, or a join. Strip B appears to stand directly BELOW
strip A in both areas (tentative; based on the enumeration "P(ri)mo ... S(e)c(un)do"
at the end of strip A's right area being followed by "Tercio ... Quarto ...
Q(ui)nto" in strip B's, and on the bottom margin in strip B). Whether any lines
are lost between the two strips I cannot say; the top line of each strip is cut
through.

Areas selected: all visible text on both strips was read. Unread: only what is
cut, abraded, or under the white paper/paste residue (marked).

Conventions: (..) = my expansion; word(?) = uncertain; [illegible] = unreadable;
[ or ] at a line edge = text cut by the edge of the strip; (Christ..) renders the
"x" with suprascript sign; neumes are not transcribed, only noted.

====================================================================
2. STRIP A, LEFT AREA (notated) - image-002
====================================================================
image-002 L1   ]e monum(en)to(?) [..] h[..] [illegible]          [upper halves cut away; very uncertain]
image-002 L2   medicamina demus . Cur estis tristes q[             [right end under white residue]
image-002 L3   queritis hic mulieres . Querimus hi[                [last word cut: "hic"/"hu.."]
image-002 L4   ih(esu)m quem novimus e(ss)e sepultum .
image-002 L5   Si surrexisset dic nobis nam ti[
image-002 L6   [..] s[.. residue ..] [..]erit(?) nolite            [lower halves cut; "nolite" clear]
Neumes stand above every syllable of L2-L6. In L5 a small group of dots forming a
triangle stands above "nam".

====================================================================
3. STRIP A, RIGHT AREA (prose) - image-003
====================================================================
image-003 L1   linguis . Vel alit(er) sp(iritu)s(?) d(omi)ni rep(?)[..]it(?) orbe(m)(?) t[   [upper halves cut]
image-003 L2   (con)tinet om(n)ia id est sp(iritu)s s(an)c(tu)s . q(uod)(?) sic ipsa divinita[
image-003 L3   op(er)ata est . sic facta p(er) sp(iritu)m s(an)c(tu)m h(abe)nt existe[
image-003 L4   o(?)[..] om(n)is virt(us) eor(um) . scia(m) (with stroke) h(abe)t vocis . v(el) fac(it) h(abe)re .
image-003 L5   sp(iritu)s postulat p(ro) nob(is) . v(el) postulare fac(it) . Is(?) e[        [end damaged; a large V-like letter at the edge]
image-003 L6   Pet(rus) damiani . liba (with stroke) inu(?)[..]tores(?) clericor(um) . V[     [enlarged initial P in margin]
image-003 L7   sac(ri)ficiu(m) d(omi)ni circu(m) volantes arripitis[
image-003 L8   fuerant crudelit(er) devoratis . Vos tig(?)[..]d(?)[
image-003 L9   ciunt p(ro)p(ter) humanu(m) sanguine(m) cruenta[
image-003 L10  Petr(us) q(ui)nq(ue) causis tonsura(m) accep(it) . P(ri)mo ut [               [enlarged initial P in margin]
image-003 L11  nea(m) corona(m) (Christi) . S(e)c(un)do ut clerici a laici[

Notes: L6, word 4: minims only, could be read "inuitores", "imitatores" or
similar; I leave it open. L6 word 3 "liba" with an abbreviation stroke is not
resolved. L8 last word begins "tig" with a suprascript sign and is cut.
Each line is cut at the right by the edge of the strip (a few letters lost at
most, to judge from the line lengths).

====================================================================
4. STRIP B, LEFT AREA - image-005
====================================================================
Notated text (same hand as strip A left):
image-005 L1   ]cr[                                                [only two letters at the torn upper left]
image-005 L2   [..]ecessit . E[.. lost under white residue ..] vacuus      [first word perhaps "p(re)cessit"/"recessit"]
image-005 L3   [..]at positus . [.. lost under residue ..][..]tio(?) rem[
image-005 L4   vos p(re)venit(?) in galileam .                     [verb written "p" with a mark above + "uenit"]
Neumes above L2-L4.

Added lines in a different, smaller cursive hand, no neumes (description of an
addition: written in the space under the notated text, lighter ink, sloping):
image-005 L5   ]it ie(su)s(?) discipulis suis(?)                    [an orange-brown smear over the last word]
image-005 L6   ]atu(m) est nosce(?) mist(?)[..]riu(m)(?) [..] cet(er)is autem in parab(olis)(?)   [smear over the middle; a small "s"-like sign above the gap]
The beginnings of L5-L6 are hidden under the leather strip at the left.

====================================================================
5. STRIP B, RIGHT AREA (prose) - image-006
====================================================================
image-006 L1   cretione(m)(?) [illegible] e[..]t(?) . Tercio ut sacerdotes vet(er)is testa[   [first words abraded/cut at top]
image-006 L2   p(ro)baret . suscipiendo tonsura(m) in illa parte capit[
image-006 L3   columba sup(er) cap(ut) (Christi) descendit . Quarto ut derisio[
image-006 L4   gannatura(m) i(n) regno romano susceptu(m)(?) . p(ro) (Christo) sustin[        [the ending of "suscept.." is an abbreviation sign I am unsure of]
image-006 L5   Q(ui)nto ut a simone mago disc(er)n(er)et(?) (Christi)anor(um) tonsor(?) i . [  [enlarged Q; verb written "disc" + stroke + "net"]
image-006 L6   capite cesaries ab aure ad aure(m) tonsa est . in a[
image-006 L7   parte . cu(m) an (with stroke) magi in fronte c(ir)cu(m)(?) habebant . In c[
image-006 L8   pite arula(?) l(?) ab sub aure ad aure(m) ducta p(er) fronte(m)
image-006 L9   [..]ando pendebat . cu(m) an (with stroke) magi i(n) sola fronte habeb[
               [blank lower margin; three or four thin descending pen strokes below L9]

Notes: "an" with a stroke (L7, L9) left unexpanded. L8 "arula" followed by a tall
letter (l or t with stroke) and "ab" with a dot under it - possibly a marked
correction/expunction of "ab" before "sub"; I describe it rather than resolve it.
L1 begins mid-word ("...cretione(m)"), consistent with a continuation from the
cut last line of strip A's right area, but I do not supply the missing letters.

====================================================================
6. LIMITATIONS
====================================================================
- Top line of each strip is cut through; strip A's bottom line (left area) is
  cut through. Right-hand line ends of the prose area are trimmed in both strips.
- White paper/paste residue hides parts of image-002 L2-L3 and L6 and much of
  image-005 L2-L3.
- The relationship of left and right areas (one leaf or two; column order) and
  the exact vertical relation of strip A to strip B are not established by the
  images. The other side of the strips is not shown.
- Neumes were observed but not transcribed; an image at higher magnification
  would be needed to describe them sign by sign.
- A view with the leather strip lifted at the left of strip B would recover the
  beginnings of the two added cursive lines.

This is an unverified image reading.

Reader activity: opened PROMPT.md and
image-001.jpg through image-006.jpg (all six).
I did not open packet.json or any other file.
